scores.evidence: The text is consistently in です・ます and warm, with no pressure phrases; steps and feedback read like a tutor sitting beside you (p-interview troubleshoot 「コードはまだ不要です。質問だけしてください」, pq1 feedback). Only a few small stiff spots remain (pq1 hint, pq5 explanation), and they are niceToHave.

lessons:lint --strict is clean, so every sentence and paragraph is within budget. Each practice section breaks into steps, prompt blocks, a checklist or an inline quiz, so there is no run of text-only screens.

The prerequisite chapter is stated, and practice-recap recalls MoSCoW before it is used. 壁打ち is defined at first use in p-interview and matches the glossary. However, summary-next uses the abbreviation 「VS Code」 for the first time in the course so far without spelling it out.

Both locales are complete, including the diagram labels, alt text and description. The prompt-block label 「期待される結果」/"What a good answer looks like" quoted in practice-tip matches the UI in PromptBlock.tsx. One English option in pq1 (「keep adding items as a Must」) can be read differently from the jp text.

mustFix.issue: (a) meaning: pq1 option a en "Move only the sorting to Should; keep adding items as a Must" can be read as 'continue adding items as Musts'. The jp 「品物の追加はMustに残す」 means keep the feature 'add items' under Must, and this is the correct answer, so the ambiguity matters.
mustFix.fix: pq1 option a en: 「Move only the sorting to Should; keep adding items as a Must」→「Move only the sorting to Should; keep "add items" as a Must」

mustFix.issue: (d) rule, style-guide §2 (略語は初出で正式名を書きます): 「VS Code」 appears here for the first time (it does not occur in ch0–ch2) and is not spelled out.
mustFix.fix: jp: 「第3章では、AIと開発するためのVS Codeを準備します。」→「第3章では、AIと開発するためのVS Code（Visual Studio Code）を準備します。」; en: 「In Chapter 3 you'll set up VS Code for building with an AI.」→「In Chapter 3 you'll set up VS Code (Visual Studio Code) for building with an AI.」

niceToHave: practice-check: the pq1 hint has two を-clauses in a row and reads stiffly — 「指摘を受け入れるかどうかを、何を物差しにして決めるか考えましょう。」→「指摘を受け入れるかどうかを決める物差しは何か、考えましょう。」
practice-plan-check: the goal in pq5 is already one sentence, so 「1文に直して」 is slightly off; name the checklist form instead — 「目的を1文に直してから、ほかの項目も見直します。」→「目的を「誰が・どんな場面で・どうなれる」の1文に直してから、ほかの項目も見直します。」

check-quiz: in pq3 en the same thing is called both "show a recipe" (Must) and "recipe view" (flow), while jp uses 「レシピの表示」 for both — 「the screen flow is "recipe list → recipe view"」→「the screen flow is "recipe list → show a recipe"」

practice-plan-check: pq5 option a en drops 「やらないことの」, which tells the learner where the item sits — 「Delete "look up sorting rules" from the plan」→「Delete "look up sorting rules" from what we won't build」

hook-b1: the en comparison is slightly off (an organizer cannot follow the 'steps as an app') — 「follows the same steps as Chapter 2's budget app」→「follows the same steps as the budget app in Chapter 2」
lesson (objectives o3 en): 'beyond the Musts too' is awkward — 「with MoSCoW, beyond the Musts too, and judge」→「with MoSCoW, including the groups other than Must, and judge」
glossary: the definition endings are mixed; 壁打ち and 1枚企画書 end in a noun 「…こと。」「…文書。」, while MoSCoW uses です・ます — 「自分の考えを言葉にしていくこと。」→「自分の考えを言葉にしていくことです。」, 「…やらないことを1枚に並べた文書。」→「…やらないことを1枚に並べた文書です。」

practice-flow: style-guide §4 asks for one sentence near a figure that says what it shows; the diagram follows practice-tip without an introduction. Consider adding a lead line before it, e.g. 「下の図は、上の企画書例のMustと画面の流れをつないだものです。」

lesson (title jp): 「第2章 演習｜…」 has a half-width space, while the other chapter titles use 「第N章｜…」 with no space; check this against the course's naming for practice lessons — 「第2章 演習｜」→「第2章演習｜」 if the course has no convention for it.

check-quiz: pq4 option c en 'keep it from the AI' suggests hiding something, while jp 「AIには渡さない」 means not handing it over — 「Rewrite the whole plan yourself and keep it from the AI」→「Rewrite the whole plan yourself without the AI」
summary: The Japanese is natural, warm and within every budget. Terms are consistent across the steps, prompt titles, diagram labels and checklist, and the prompt-block label quoted in practice-tip matches the UI. Two fixes remain before the lesson passes: make the ambiguous English correct option in pq1 (practice-check) unambiguous, and spell out VS Code (Visual Studio Code) at its first use in summary-next.
